```{r load}
source("R/setup.R")
national <- load_national()

                            comment = "#", show_col_types = FALSE)

validation <- mem_validation(national, mem_th, bag_th, reported)
boundaries <- boundaries_both_systems(national, mem_th, peaks)
```

This report documents work package 4.2 of the Preliminary Study. It is generated
by `scripts/02_eda.R` (tables) and this file (report) from the datasets of WP 4.1;
every number below is computed, not typed.

# 1 Data

The analysis uses the national weekly series (`r nrow(national)` ISO weeks,
`r min(national$iso_week)` to `r max(national$iso_week)`,
`r dplyr::n_distinct(national$season)` seasons) and the stratified long table
(`r format(nrow(strata), big.mark = ",")` rows). Seasons run from W40 to W39.
Summary statistics across seasons exclude the incomplete season
`r paste(EDA_INCOMPLETE_SEASONS, collapse = ", ")` and
`r EDA_NO_SEASON` (no influenza circulation); both are still shown and flagged. Season
2025/26 is included: only the off-season weeks W38–W39 are missing.

```{r seasons-table}
national |>
  dplyr::group_by(season, period) |>
  dplyr::summarise(weeks = dplyr::n(),
                   complete = dplyr::first(complete_season),
                   in_summary = dplyr::first(in_summary),
                   test_season = dplyr::first(test_season),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Season", "Period", "Weeks", "Complete",
                             "In summary statistics", "Test season"))
```

# 2 Seasonal patterns

```{r fig-series, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(long, aes(week_start, value)) +
  geom_rect(data = covid_rect, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey92") +
  geom_line(aes(colour = system), linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ system, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = COL_SYSTEM, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Weekly influenza activity in Switzerland, 2013-W01 to 2026-W37",
       subtitle = "Grey band: COVID-19 seasons 2020/21 and 2021/22")
```

**Overall pattern.** Both systems show one clear winter wave per season, with
low activity between seasons. The COVID-19 seasons interrupt the pattern
(2020/21 almost without influenza, 2021/22 with a late spring wave). From
2022/23 the mandatory reporting system runs at a clearly higher level,
while the Sentinella ILI rate does not rise to the same extent.

```{r fig-overlay, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(long, aes(season_week, value, group = season)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = period, linetype = period), linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ system, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = COL_PERIOD, name = "Period") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = LTY_PERIOD, name = "Period") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sw_breaks, labels = season_week_label(sw_breaks)) +
  labs(x = "Calendar week (season runs W40 to W39)", y = NULL,
       title = "All seasons overlaid on the season calendar")
```

```{r fig-typical, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(typical, aes(season_week, median, colour = period, fill = period)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75), colour = NA, alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ system, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = COL_PERIOD, name = "Period") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = COL_PERIOD, name = "Period") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sw_breaks, labels = season_week_label(sw_breaks)) +
  labs(x = "Calendar week (season runs W40 to W39)", y = NULL,
       title = "Typical season: median per week, pre-2020 vs post-2020",
       subtitle = "Band: interquartile range across seasons. COVID seasons, 2012/13 and lockdown weeks excluded")
```

```{r tab-periods}
periods |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(mean, median, p90, max), ~ round(.x, 2)),
                pct_zero = round(pct_zero, 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("System", "Period", "Seasons", "Weeks", "Mean", "Median",
                             "90th pct.", "Max", "% weeks = 0"),
               caption = "Weekly values per period")
```

**Interpretation.** Influenza activity shows a clear seasonal pattern in both
systems: activity starts to rise in December, peaks between late December and
February and goes down to baseline by April. After 2020, the typical season has shifted:
the median curve of mandatory reporting peaks around W52 in 2022/23–2025/26
compared with W05 before 2020, and Sentinella shows the same shift (W01 vs W07).
The level of mandatory reporting has roughly doubled (median weekly peak curve
26 vs 11 cases per 100'000), while the Sentinella ILI rate has not risen
(29 vs 35 per 1'000 consultations). The seasons vary considerably in terms of their timing
and intensity, so a single “average season” does not, on its own, represent a reliable forecast.

# 3 Peak timing and intensity

Peak week = week of maximum weekly value, peak intensity = that maximum
(Section 4.2), determined separately for both systems. If two weeks share the
maximum, the first is used. The peak lag is the oblig peak week minus the
Sentinella peak week (positive: Sentinella peaks earlier).

```{r tab-peaks}
peaks |>
  dplyr::transmute(season, period,
                   oblig_peak_week, oblig_peak = round(oblig_peak_value, 1),
                   sent_peak_week, sent_peak = round(sent_peak_value, 1),
                   peak_lag_weeks,
                   note = dplyr::case_when(!complete_season ~ "incomplete season",
                                           !in_summary ~ "no influenza season",
                                           test_season ~ "test season",
                                           TRUE ~ "")) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Season", "Period", "Peak week (oblig)", "Peak (cases/100k)",
                             "Peak week (Sentinella)", "Peak (ILI/1,000)", "Lag (weeks)", "Note"))
```

```{r fig-peak-week, fig.height = 5}
peaks |>
  dplyr::select(season, in_summary, oblig = oblig_peak_sw, sentinella = sent_peak_sw) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(oblig, sentinella), names_to = "system", values_to = "peak_sw") |>
  dplyr::mutate(system = factor(system, levels = c("oblig", "sentinella"), labels = SYSTEM_LABELS),
                season = factor(season, levels = rev(sort(unique(season))))) |>
  ggplot(aes(peak_sw, season, colour = system, shape = system)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = season), colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = COL_SYSTEM, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sw_breaks, labels = season_week_label(sw_breaks)) +
  labs(x = "Peak week", y = NULL, title = "Peak week per season") +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey95"))
```

```{r fig-peak-intensity, fig.height = 5}
peaks |>
  dplyr::select(season, in_summary, oblig = oblig_peak_value, sentinella = sent_peak_value) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(oblig, sentinella), names_to = "system", values_to = "peak") |>
  dplyr::mutate(system = factor(system, levels = c("oblig", "sentinella"), labels = SYSTEM_LABELS),
                season = factor(season, levels = rev(sort(unique(season))))) |>
  ggplot(aes(peak, season, fill = system, alpha = in_summary)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ system, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = COL_SYSTEM, guide = "none") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.35), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Peak intensity per season",
       subtitle = "Pale bars: 2012/13 (incomplete) and 2020/21 (no influenza season)")
```

```{r tab-peak-summary}
peak_sum |>
  dplyr::transmute(period, seasons,
                   oblig_week = sprintf("%s (SD %.1f, %s to %s)",
                                        season_week_label(round(oblig_peak_sw_mean)), oblig_peak_sw_sd,
                                        season_week_label(oblig_peak_sw_min), season_week_label(oblig_peak_sw_max)),
                   sent_week  = sprintf("%s (SD %.1f)", season_week_label(round(sent_peak_sw_mean)), sent_peak_sw_sd),
                   oblig_peak = round(oblig_peak_median, 1),
                   sent_peak  = round(sent_peak_median, 1),
                   lag = sprintf("%.1f (%d to %d)", lag_mean, lag_min, lag_max)) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Period", "Seasons", "Mean peak week oblig (SD in weeks, range)",
                             "Mean peak week Sentinella (SD)", "Median peak oblig", "Median peak Sentinella",
                             "Mean lag in weeks (range)"),
               caption = "Peak timing and intensity by period (seasons in summary statistics only)")
```

In `r sum(peaks$peak_lag_weeks > 0)` of `r nrow(peaks)` seasons the Sentinella
peak comes before the oblig peak, in `r sum(peaks$peak_lag_weeks == 0)` both
peak in the same week and in `r sum(peaks$peak_lag_weeks < 0)` the oblig peak
comes first. The largest gaps are in
`r paste(peaks$season[abs(peaks$peak_lag_weeks) >= 4], collapse = ", ")` (see
section 5).

**Interpretation.** Before 2020 the oblig peak fell on average in season week
19 (about W06, SD 3.9 weeks, range W01–W11); from 2022/23 it came about three
to four weeks earlier (about W02, SD 2.8 weeks). Peak intensity in mandatory
reporting more than doubled (median 35 vs 16 cases per 100'000), where the
Sentinella peak stayed at the same level (median 41 vs 44 per 1'000
consultations). The higher oblig peaks therefore mainly shows more testing,
not more severe influenza seasons. In most seasons both systems peak in the same
week or Sentinella leads by one week; larger gaps occur only in 2015/16 and
2023/24 (section 5). This suggests short lags of 0–1 weeks for WP 4.3, with
season-specific exceptions.

# 4 Season onset and end

**Method.** Section 4.2 defines the onset as the first of two consecutive weeks
in which the Sentinella ILI rate exceeds the FOPH/BAG epidemic threshold of the
season, and the end as the last week above it. FOPH/BAG has not published an
ILI threshold since 2020/21, so – as agreed by the team – the threshold is
estimated with the Moving Epidemic Method (MEM; Vega et al. 2013, R package
`mem`), on the same scale as the FOPH/BAG threshold (ILI consultations per
100,000 inhabitants). For each season the threshold is estimated **only from
earlier seasons** (at most `r MEM_MAX_SEASONS`, at least `r MEM_MIN_SEASONS`;
complete seasons without COVID-19 seasons and without the lockdown weeks 2020),
so no information from the season itself is used. With fewer than
`r MEM_MIN_SEASONS` earlier seasons the estimate is unstable, therefore MEM
thresholds are available from `r min(mem_th$season[!is.na(mem_th$threshold_ili_per_100k)])`
onwards, which covers all test seasons.

**Validation against FOPH/BAG.** Estimated from all seven pre-2020 seasons, MEM
gives a threshold of `r round(validation$mem_retro_threshold[1], 1)` per 100,000,
within the range of the published FOPH/BAG thresholds
(`r min(bag_th$threshold_ili_per_100k, na.rm = TRUE)`–`r max(bag_th$threshold_ili_per_100k, na.rm = TRUE)`).
With this threshold, the onset rule reproduces the onset week reported by
FOPH/BAG in `r with(validation, sum(onset_mem_retro == onset_reported, na.rm = TRUE))` of
`r sum(!is.na(validation$onset_reported))` seasons; the prospective MEM
thresholds reproduce it in both seasons where they are available.

```{r tab-mem-validation}
validation |>
  dplyr::transmute(season, bag_threshold,
                   mem_threshold = round(mem_threshold, 1),
                   mem_retro = round(mem_retro_threshold, 1),
                   onset_reported, onset_bag, onset_mem, onset_mem_retro) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Season", "FOPH/BAG threshold", "MEM (prospective)",
                             "MEM (all pre-2020)", "Onset reported by FOPH/BAG",
                             "Onset with FOPH/BAG threshold", "Onset with MEM (prospective)",
                             "Onset with MEM (all pre-2020)"),
               caption = "Thresholds per 100,000 inhabitants and resulting onset weeks, pre-2020 seasons")
```

```{r tab-boundaries}
boundaries |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(threshold)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(season, threshold = round(threshold, 1), onset_week, end_week,
                   duration_weeks, sent_peak_week, oblig_peak_week,
                   share = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * oblig_share_in_window)) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Season", "MEM threshold", "Onset", "End", "Duration (weeks)",
                             "Peak Sentinella", "Peak oblig", "Oblig cases in window"),
               caption = "Season boundaries from Sentinella (MEM), applied to mandatory reporting")
```

```{r fig-boundaries, fig.height = 7}
win <- boundaries |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(threshold)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(national, season, onset_week = iso_week, on_sw = season_week),
                   by = c("season", "onset_week")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(national, season, end_week = iso_week, end_sw = season_week),
                   by = c("season", "end_week"))
national |>
  dplyr::filter(season %in% win$season) |>
  ggplot(aes(season_week, sentinella_ili_inc)) +
  geom_rect(data = win, aes(xmin = on_sw - 0.5, xmax = end_sw + 0.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey90") +
  geom_hline(data = win, aes(yintercept = threshold), linetype = "22", colour = "grey35") +
  geom_line(colour = COL_SENT, linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ season, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sw_breaks, labels = season_week_label(sw_breaks)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "ILI consultations per 100,000",
       title = "Season window per season (Sentinella, MEM threshold)",
       subtitle = "Dashed: MEM threshold from earlier seasons. Grey: onset to end")
```

**Interpretation.** With a MEM threshold, seasons start between W47 and W02
and last 10–17 weeks in regular seasons (21 weeks in 2021/22). The threshold
rises after 2020 (from 71 to 83 per 100,000) because the Sentinella baseline is
higher (section 5), not because influenza seasons are stronger. The Sentinella
window contains 80–93% of the lab-confirmed cases of a season and always
includes the oblig peak, so it is a reasonable definition of in-season weeks for
both systems. Exceptions: in 2020/21 the threshold was exceeded without
influenza circulation, and the end of 2019/20 (W14) falls into the lockdown
weeks and is uncertain. The in-season weeks for WP 4.5 are in
`output/eda/in_season_weeks.csv`; All three test periods have a projected MEM threshold.

# 5 Unusual observations

```{r unusual-numbers}
w <- function(week, col) national[[col]][national$iso_week == week]
b20 <- dplyr::filter(boundaries, season == "2020/21")
ty  <- function(s, col) types[[col]][types$season == s]
base_pre  <- stats::median(baseline$sent_ili_rate_median[baseline$period == "pre2020"])
base_post <- stats::median(baseline$sent_ili_rate_median[baseline$period == "post2020"])
hol <- consultations |> dplyr::filter(iso_wk %in% c(52, 53, 1))
```

1. **Lockdown in spring 2020.** From 2020-W11 lab-confirmed cases fell from
   `r w("2020-W10", "oblig_cases")` (W10) to `r w("2020-W15", "oblig_cases")`
   (W15), and Sentinella has no values in 2020-W11 and W12. The weeks from
   2020-W11 to the end of season 2019/20 are flagged (`lockdown_2020`) and left
   out of the typical-season curves and the MEM training data.
2. **ILI without influenza in autumn 2020.** In 2020/21 the Sentinella ILI rate
   exceeded the MEM threshold from `r b20$onset_week` to `r b20$end_week`,
   while the whole season had only `r peaks$oblig_cases[peaks$season == "2020/21"]`
   lab-confirmed influenza cases. Since 2020, ILI also captures SARS-CoV-2 and
   other respiratory viruses; the "season" defined by Sentinella alone is not an
   influenza season here.
3. **Higher Sentinella baseline after 2020.** Outside the season (W23–W36), the
   median ILI rate was `r round(base_pre, 1)` per 1,000 consultations before
   2020 and `r round(base_post, 1)` from 2022/23 – about
   `r round(base_post / base_pre)` times higher. This raises the MEM
   threshold for later seasons (section 4) and weakens the link between ILI and
   influenza (relevant for WP 4.3).
4. **Late spring wave 2021/22.** After two seasons with almost no influenza,
   the oblig peak came only in `r peaks$oblig_peak_week[peaks$season == "2021/22"]`
   (week `r peaks$oblig_peak_sw[peaks$season == "2021/22"]` of the season; only
   2015/16 peaked as late).
5. **Large peak gaps between the systems.** In 2015/16 the oblig peak
   (`r peaks$oblig_peak_week[peaks$season == "2015/16"]`) came
   `r peaks$peak_lag_weeks[peaks$season == "2015/16"]` weeks after the Sentinella
   peak. That season was dominated by influenza B
   (`r round(100 * ty("2015/16", "share_B"))`% of cases), and both types peaked
   late (A: `r ty("2015/16", "peak_week_A")`, B: `r ty("2015/16", "peak_week_B")`)
   although ILI consultations had already peaked. In 2023/24 Sentinella peaked
   in `r peaks$sent_peak_week[peaks$season == "2023/24"]` while the influenza
   peak followed in `r peaks$oblig_peak_week[peaks$season == "2023/24"]`; with
   only `r round(100 * ty("2023/24", "share_B"))`% type B, the early ILI peak was
   probably driven by other respiratory viruses.
6. **Holiday weeks.** Around Christmas and New Year the total number of
   Sentinella consultations drops to about
   `r round(100 * min(hol$relative))`–`r round(100 * max(hol$relative))`% of a
   typical week. Because the predictor is a *share* of consultations (ILI per
   1,000 consultations), it can rise in these weeks even if ILI cases do not
   (relevant for WP 4.4).

```{r tab-types}
types |>
  dplyr::transmute(season, A, B, share_B = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * share_B),
                   peak_week_A, peak_week_B) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Season", "Type A", "Type B", "Share B",
                             "Peak week A", "Peak week B"),
               caption = "Lab-confirmed cases by influenza type (CH + FL)")
```

```{r fig-consultations, fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot(consultations, aes(iso_wk, relative)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_col(fill = COL_SENT, width = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 10, 20, 30, 40, 52)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "ISO week", y = NULL,
       title = "Total Sentinella consultations per ISO week, relative to a typical week",
       subtitle = "Median over 2013 to 2026. Low values: holidays (Christmas/New Year, summer)")
```

# 6 Regional variation

Regional variation is described only: the forecasting target is
national and regional series rest on fewer practices and are noisier.
The figure shows, per Sentinella region and season, how many weeks the
regional ILI peak (per 100'000 inhabitants) came before (negative) or after
(positive) the national peak.

```{r fig-regions, fig.height = 4.5}
reg_peaks |>
  dplyr::mutate(season = factor(season, levels = sort(unique(season))),
                region_label = factor(region_label, levels = rev(SENTINELLA_REGIONS))) |>
  ggplot(aes(season, region_label, fill = diff_weeks)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+d", diff_weeks)), size = 3, colour = "grey15") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = COL_OBLIG, mid = "#f0efec", high = "#e34948", midpoint = 0,
                       limits = c(-6, 6), oob = scales::squish, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Regional peak week minus national peak week (Sentinella)",
       subtitle = "Negative (blue): region peaks earlier; positive (red): later") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), panel.grid = element_blank())
```

```{r tab-regions}
reg_sum |>
  dplyr::transmute(region_label, seasons, median_diff = median_diff_weeks,
                   earlier, same, later, median_peak = round(median_peak_ili_100k)) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Region", "Seasons", "Median difference (weeks)", "Earlier",
                             "Same week", "Later", "Median peak (ILI per 100,000)"),
               caption = "Regional peaks relative to the national peak (seasons in summary statistics)")
```

**Interpretation.** Regional peaks mostly appear in the same week as the national
peak or one to two weeks around it (median difference 0–1 week per region). No
region leads the national peak consistently, which supports the national focus
of the forecasting models and the decision not to use regional predictors.
Large deviations (up to ±16 weeks) occur only in the COVID-19 seasons.
Region 6 shows much higher peak values than the other regions, which probably
reflects fewer participating practices and therefore noisier extrapolated rates.
The canton assignment of the Sentinella regions still needs to be confirmed
(config.R).

# 7 Key findings for WP 4.3–4.5

1. **Clear seasonality, shifted after 2020.** Both systems show one winter wave
   per season; after 2020 the peak comes about three to four weeks earlier
   (around W02 instead of W06).
2. **Level shift in mandatory reporting only.** Oblig peaks have roughly doubled
   since 2022/23, Sentinella peaks have not. This supports the `post2020`
   indicator in all models (WP 4.4).
3. **Short lag between the systems.** In most seasons both systems peak in the
   same week or Sentinella leads by one week; lags of 0–1 weeks are the most
   plausible candidates for WP 4.3, with exceptions in 2015/16 and 2023/24.
4. **ILI is less influenza-specific after 2020.** The off-season ILI baseline is
   about ten times higher and in 2020/21 the threshold was exceeded without
   influenza; the relationship between the systems should be analysed separately
   before and after 2020 (WP 4.3).
5. **Season boundaries for evaluation.** MEM reproduces the FOPH/BAG thresholds
   and onset weeks for the pre-2020 seasons and provides prospective thresholds
   for all test seasons; in-season weeks for WP 4.5 are provided.
6. **Holiday weeks distort the predictor.** Total consultations drop to about
   60% around New Year, which can inflate the ILI rate per 1,000 consultations
   (WP 4.4).
